title.en: The Attorney General and the Supreme Court

text.en: On 28 January 1950 a new court was inaugurated in New Delhi. It succeeded the Federal Court of 1935 and was named the Guardian of the Constitution.

Article 76 provides for the Attorney General, the highest law officer of India, appointed by the President and removable by him.
He advises the government on legal matters, has the right to appear in all courts, and may speak in Parliament but cannot vote.
The judiciary is the third organ of government and protects the rights and freedoms of citizens.
India has an integrated judiciary, a single judicial hierarchy for the whole country.
In 1950 the Supreme Court had 8 judges, including the Chief Justice.
The Chief Justice is appointed by the President, and other judges in consultation with the collegium headed by the Chief Justice.
A judge must be a citizen who has served as a High Court judge for five years, or as a High Court advocate for ten years, or be a distinguished jurist.
Judges hold office up to the age of 65, and Parliament can remove them by impeachment.
Original jurisdiction covers disputes between the Centre and states, between states, and writs for fundamental rights.
Appellate jurisdiction makes it the final court of appeal in civil, criminal and constitutional cases.
Advisory jurisdiction lets the President refer questions of law or fact of public importance.
Judicial review is the power to examine whether a law is unconstitutional.
The law declared by the Supreme Court binds all courts in India.

problem.en: Explain the original and appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

text.en: Original jurisdiction: cases come directly to the Supreme Court.

why.en: Disputes between the Centre and states, or between states.

text.en: It also issues writs for fundamental rights.
Appellate jurisdiction: it hears appeals from High Courts in civil, criminal and constitutional cases.

why.en: It is the final court of appeal.

requiredIdeas.en: Power to examine if a law is constitutional
Laws against the Constitution are struck down

points.en: Attorney General: Article 76, highest law officer.
Jurisdictions: original, appellate, advisory, judicial review.
